answer: The cheapest real defence: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because lagoon only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, nebula is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any basalt approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
